newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Leighton sees higher yr profit and sales.
newsitem.headline: Leighton sees higher yr profit and sales.

text.p: Construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Friday it remained confident of higher earnings and sales in 1996/97 (July-June).
"During the quarter, good progress was made on the broad range of projects being undertaken by the group," chief executive Wal King said in the third quarter report.
"Following the strong first half result, we are confident that operating profit for the full year will substantially exceed last year's A$65 million operating profit," King said.

"Whilst the sale of Welded Mesh was opportunistic in terms of accepting an attractive offer for the business, it also signals that we are moving towards the end of a phase of divestment of non-core assets," he said.
"Our core construction, mining and property operations should maintain a good level of activity over the next few years and the group is in an enviable position of financial strength.
"We are now initiating a planning process to ensure we sustain growth and maximise returns to shareholders in the longer term," King said.
"A high level of activity continued throughout the group during the third quarter of 1996/97 with annual operating revenue on track to exceed last year," King also said.
"The high level of uncompleted work in hand remains steady at A$3.3 billion."
King also said the A$140 million sale of its Welded Mesh unit to Smorgon Steel announced in April would generate a net abnormal profit of about A$48 million.
